title: "agent"

Use `setupmjr agent` for user-level coding-agent configuration. `pj` launches already-configured agents; provider and credential setup belongs here.

Install all three CLIs with `setupmjr install agents` (see [installation](install.qmd#coding-agent-clis)). It uses the existing native vendor installers, skips CLIs already on `PATH`, and leaves authentication, API credentials and configured model providers unchanged.

Run `setupmjr agent --help` for authoritative option syntax and `setupmjr agent --list` for accepted endpoints, providers, subagents and aliases.

## Inspect configuration

```bash
setupmjr agent --config
setupmjr agent --list
```

`--config` reports the effective Codex provider, Copilot provider and configured opt-in subagent. Running `setupmjr agent` without options prints command help.

## Update installed CLIs

```bash
setupmjr agent update claude
setupmjr agent update codex
setupmjr agent update copilot
setupmjr agent update --all
```

Choose one agent or `--all`; these selectors cannot be combined with provider or authentication options. Updates use the first matching executable on PATH. With `--all`, missing tools are reported as skipped; a missing single selection is an error. Every installed tool is attempted even if another fails, with a separate completion or failure line for each tool and a nonzero exit status if any failed. Vendor output reports whether a version changed or was already current; completion means the update command succeeded.

| Installed method | Update path |
| --- | --- |
| Native Claude, Codex or Copilot on Linux, macOS, WSL or Windows | The installed CLI's `update` command, after checking its help advertises that command |
| Homebrew executable resolving into `Caskroom` or `Cellar` | `brew upgrade --cask <installed-package>` or `brew upgrade --formula <installed-package>` |
| Claude or Copilot resolving into a Windows WinGet package directory | `winget upgrade --id <installed-package> --exact --source winget` |
| Detected npm/shim, system `/usr/bin` or `/bin`, or Nix installation | Report an error directing you to the original package manager |

Homebrew package suffixes and Copilot's WinGet prerelease package are retained. An installed package manager must be on PATH. Other custom wrappers or install layouts may not reveal their package manager; native update support and installation handling are then delegated to the vendor. Older CLIs without an advertised `update` command require a one-time update through their original installer or package manager. setupmjr does not automatically migrate them to another installation method.

An explicit update requests a manual check even when background updates are available. Existing auto-update settings, environment variables and release-channel configuration are passed through. setupmjr does not rewrite provider configuration, sign-in state, credentials or shell startup files. Vendor updaters may use the network, request permissions, and require running agent sessions to be restarted. On WSL, use the Linux setupmjr and Linux agents. Platforms other than Linux, macOS and Windows are rejected.

See the official [Claude update documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup#update-claude-code), [Codex command reference](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference#codex-update), and [Copilot command reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-command-reference).

## Diagnose installations

```bash
setupmjr agent doctor
```

Doctor checks Claude Code (`claude`), Codex (`codex`) and GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`) on the current process's PATH. It prints the selected executable locations, versions and setupmjr-managed provider/subagent configuration, then continues through all checks with actionable fixes. It exits **0** when no checks fail and **1** when any check fails, including a missing CLI. `WARN` means unverified and does not change the exit status. Extra options are rejected; doctor cannot be combined with setup actions.

Checks are read-only: doctor never installs, updates, signs in, sources shell files or writes configuration. It invokes only `--version`, [Claude's `auth status`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference) and [Codex's `login status`](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference/), with closed stdin and a ten-second timeout per probe. Raw command output and errors are suppressed; only version numbers and credential-presence/status summaries are displayed. It makes no inference requests or deliberate credential-validation network requests. Local credential presence does not establish validity, account entitlement or service connectivity.

[Copilot authentication](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/authenticate-copilot-cli) may live in an OS credential store. Doctor does not inspect that store or launch an interactive session: it reports authentication as unverified when no token environment variable is available. It checks `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` in precedence order for empty values and unsupported classic PATs, without printing their values. Provider API keys are reported as present but unvalidated. To resolve access problems, run `copilot login` yourself.

Managed DeepSeek checks detect missing credentials, an inactive Copilot shell environment and incomplete isolated subagent configuration. An opted-in agy subagent must be on PATH; its authentication remains unverified. `CODEX_HOME` is honored by the Codex checks and produces a warning because it can override setupmjr's configuration in `~/.codex`. Custom providers, CLI-specific configuration overrides and credential helpers may need separate investigation.

Platform details:

- **Ubuntu/Linux and WSL:** PATH checks describe the current Linux environment. A Windows installation does not establish that the Linux CLI is available in WSL; run the Linux setupmjr executable there.
- **macOS:** the same CLI status commands support credentials stored through vendor mechanisms, including Keychain; doctor does not assume that a missing plaintext credential file means signed out.
- **Native Windows:** lookup uses Windows PATH/PATHEXT. Doctor probes native executables directly; `.cmd`/`.bat` shims produce an actionable failure asking for the native installation. Claude Code needs Git for Windows (Git Bash). Bash/Zsh exports do not configure PowerShell; configure custom provider variables in the shell that launches Copilot.

## Store DeepSeek authentication

```bash
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
setupmjr agent -a d
```

Authentication is credential-only: it does not change the active Codex or Copilot provider.

setupmjr reuses `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` when available, then checks its managed credential and existing Codex DeepSeek configuration, and otherwise prompts without echoing the key. The reusable credential is stored at:

```text
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key
```

The file is private and can be reused by both managed DeepSeek provider paths. DeepSeek is currently the only managed `--auth` endpoint.

## Copilot provider

These options configure **GitHub Copilot CLI in Bash/Zsh**, including Ubuntu/WSL. They do not configure the VS Code extension or native PowerShell.

Select a provider, then run plain `copilot`:

```bash
setupmjr agent -p openai      # aliases: -p o
# Only for first-time setup in an already-open terminal:
source ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.sh
copilot

setupmjr agent -p github      # aliases: -p, -p g
copilot                      # Copilot allowances / GitHub-managed models

setupmjr agent -p deepseek    # alias: -p d
copilot                      # DeepSeek API
```

The first selection installs a managed Bash/Zsh function named `copilot` through a bounded block in `.bashrc` and `.zshrc`. It calls the existing Copilot binary and reads the latest provider selection on every invocation. New shells load the integration automatically; a terminal already open during first-time setup needs to load `copilot.sh` once. The conditional sourcing reminder applies only to that initial setup, not to provider switches. Later selections apply to the next `copilot` invocation without restarting or sourcing again. Existing aliases and custom functions are preserved with a warning; use `type copilot` to check resolution. Calling an absolute binary path or `command copilot` bypasses the managed function.

The non-secret selection is stored in `~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env`, with the function in `copilot.sh`. Both files are mode `0600` in the managed `0700` directory on POSIX. Selection writes are atomic, and non-regular file targets are rejected. The binary is never replaced. Do not source `copilot.env` directly; it is read inside the function's isolated child environment.

### OpenAI API: Sol 6.1

The function reads an exported `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_KEY` from the terminal that runs `copilot`; `OPENAI_API_KEY` takes precedence when nonempty. If your key is already exported, no additional export is needed. For an existing shell-local variable, use `export OPENAI_KEY` without pasting its value into a command. No key is copied to a setupmjr configuration or shell file. Missing keys stop launch without falling back to Copilot allowances.

For the current source checkout before installation/release:

```bash
cd /home/mrodo/repos/setupmjr
go run ./cmd/setupmjr agent -p openai
source ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.sh
copilot
```

Use the same source command with `-p github` or `-p deepseek` to switch again. No special launch command is required. Any earlier placeholder provider registry is left untouched and unused.

OpenAI uses `https://api.openai.com/v1`, provider type `openai`, wire API `responses`, and `gpt-6.1-sol` with medium reasoning. Sol needs Responses for tool calling. The prompt budget is 272,000 tokens to stay within its standard input-price threshold; output is capped at 128,000. The installed Ubuntu/WSL Copilot CLI 1.0.91's local help was checked for the provider, wire API, model and reasoning flags. Launches disable automatic CLI updates.

DeepSeek reads an exported `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, otherwise the existing private credential created by `setupmjr agent --auth deepseek`. It uses the Flash model through `https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic` with wire type `anthropic`. Selecting a provider does not create or copy any API credential.

Before API launches, credential-free local help checks reject an installed CLI that does not advertise the required BYOK/Responses options and model flags. Every invocation clears stale provider endpoints, keys, bearer tokens, key commands, headers, transports, model overrides and OpenAI SDK routing overrides inside the child environment. An empty null-device named registry prevents saved registries from overriding the selected route. Returning to `github` clears BYOK routing so the CLI uses GitHub-managed access. The original OpenAI and DeepSeek key variables are removed from the child after assigning the selected provider key. Parent-shell environment and unrelated startup content are preserved. As with any environment authentication, the running child holds its selected key; the integration disables shell tracing before expanding credentials.

### Inspect the selected route

```bash
setupmjr agent copilot-status
# Or, from the source checkout:
go run ./cmd/setupmjr agent copilot-status
```

Status shows the configured provider, endpoint, wire API, model and key-presence summary. It never shows a key, prefix or hash. For an existing DeepSeek credential file, presence is based on metadata without reading its contents. `type copilot` shows whether the managed function resolves in the current terminal. `--config` includes the same routing information. Status is not proof of a completed request, valid key, actual API charge or grant-ledger allocation; selecting a model name alone does not prove billing route.

OpenAI's grant guide covers eligible organization-billed API usage and excludes Codex usage through API keys. It does not explicitly certify this Copilot integration. Use a project key from the organization linked to the grant. Purchased API credits can be consumed after a grant runs out. No account linking, credit claiming, paid probe or ledger verification occurs during setup or status checks.

Official references (checked 2026-10-29): [Copilot model providers](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-llm-models), [Sol 6.1](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol), [API credit rules](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatgpt-api-credits). The installed CLI's `copilot help providers` is the checked source for environment-based BYOK.

## Codex provider

OpenAI/ChatGPT is the default value for `-c`:

```bash
setupmjr agent -c
setupmjr agent -c o
setupmjr agent --codex-provider openai
```

Switch to DeepSeek with:

```bash
setupmjr agent -c d
setupmjr agent --codex-provider deepseek
```

The first managed DeepSeek setup uses DeepSeek's official Codex setup script and selects the Flash model. setupmjr stages that script with its bounded downloader and runs it with `bash --noprofile --norc` plus a reduced environment. A timeout, failed HTTP response or incomplete download prevents execution.

This remains a remote-code trust boundary: DeepSeek publishes the installer at a mutable CDN URL without a versioned script or checksum that setupmjr can pin. If you do not want to run the vendor script, use DeepSeek's documented manual Codex setup instead: <https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/codex/>.

Before provider changes, setupmjr snapshots the active Codex `config.toml` and `models.json` under:

```text
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/codex/
```

After both providers have been seen once, switching restores local snapshots instead of rerunning the DeepSeek installer. A pre-existing manual DeepSeek installation uses the vendor restore path once to capture the OpenAI state.

Provider changes affect the ordinary `~/.codex` home. Restart active Codex clients after switching. Restoring OpenAI configuration does not itself restore a ChatGPT login that a previous DeepSeek session may have displaced.

The automated DeepSeek bootstrap requires Bash and is intended for Linux, macOS and WSL.

## Opt-in subagent

`agy` is the default value for `-s`:

```bash
setupmjr agent -s
setupmjr agent -s agy
setupmjr agent --subagent agy
```

This installs bounded Codex guidance for explicitly authorised delegation through `agy`, preserving instructions outside the managed block.

DeepSeek can be configured instead:

```bash
setupmjr agent -s deepseek
```

The DeepSeek subagent uses the isolated Codex home `~/.codex-deepseek-subagent` and does not change the primary Codex provider. Its worker runs through `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`. Delegation remains opt-in for the current task or conversation.

Selecting one managed subagent replaces the other. `--subagent-agy` remains as a deprecated compatibility alias for `--subagent agy`.

## Credential boundaries

setupmjr creates managed agent-state directories with mode `0700` and credential/snapshot files with mode `0600` on POSIX systems. DeepSeek's Codex `config.toml` format contains the API key, so DeepSeek snapshots are credentials too. Do not commit or share the managed credential or snapshot files.
